units.title: Positive log-concavity on a domain
units.statement: Let E be a real module, s⊆E any set, and f:E→ℝ. Define positive log-concavity on s to mean that f is strictly positive at every point of s and log f is concave on s. Concavity includes convexity of s. This definition imposes no condition on f outside s.
units.formula: \operatorname{LC}_s(f)\ :\Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl[\forall x\in s,\ f(x)>0\bigr]\ \land\ \bigl[s\text{ convex and }\forall x,y\in s,\ a,b\ge0,\ a+b=1:\ a\log f(x)+b\log f(y)\le\log f(ax+by)\bigr].
assumptions: E : Type* with [AddCommMonoid E] and [Module ℝ E]. These are the exact algebraic ambient structures; no topology, norm, measure or finite-dimensionality is assumed.
s : Set E and f : E → ℝ are arbitrary; positivity and concavity are clauses of the definition, not input hypotheses.

steps.title: Require genuine positivity on the domain
steps.text: The first clause ensures that each logarithm refers to the usual logarithm of a positive real value. This excludes functions that vanish inside s; it does not rely on Lean's totalized value of log at zero or a negative number.

units.title: Every superlevel set of a positive log-concave function is convex
units.statement: Let E be a real module, f:E→ℝ positive log-concave on s⊆E, and c∈ℝ. Then S_c={x∈s:c≤f(x)} is convex. No positivity assumption on c is needed.
units.formula: S_c=\{x\in s:f(x)\ge c\},\qquad \operatorname{LC}_s(f)\Longrightarrow S_c\text{ convex for every }c\in\mathbb R.
assumptions: E : Type* with [AddCommMonoid E] and [Module ℝ E]. These are the exact algebraic ambient structures; no topology, norm, measure or finite-dimensionality is assumed.
s : Set E, f : E → ℝ, hf : LogConcaveOn s f.
c : ℝ arbitrary. In the proof x,y∈S_c and a,b≥0 with a+b=1; set z=ax+by.

steps.title: Handle nonpositive thresholds directly
steps.text: If c≤0, every point of s belongs to S_c because f is strictly positive there. For x,y∈S_c, convexity of s puts z in s and hence f(z)>0≥c. This proves the case c≤0 without taking log c.

by_cases hc : c ≤ 0
· intro x hx y hy a b ha hb hab
  have hmid_s := hf.convex_domain hx.1 hy.1 ha hb hab
  exact ⟨hmid_s, le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hc (hf.pos (x := a • x + b • y) hmid_s))⟩

steps.text: In the remaining case c is positive. Both endpoints satisfy c≤f(x),f(y), so monotonicity of log gives log c≤log f(x),log f(y). The midpoint z lies in s by domain convexity and f(z)>0.
steps.formula: \log c\le\log f(x),\quad\log c\le\log f(y),\quad z\in s,\quad f(z)>0.

steps.title: Construct the linear difference map
